learning_outcomes.text: The student knows and understands the fundamentals of vibrations.
The student, at the end of the course, will be able to identify, formulate, and solve vibration problems using the explained methods.
Furthermore, they must be able to design and perform vibration experiments, interpreting data and drawing conclusions.
Know and apply vibration analysis methods in systems with one and n degrees of freedom.
Know and apply the fundamentals of vibrations in continuous systems.
Know and apply vibration isolation techniques.
Is able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Vibrations in systems with one degree of freedom.
Vibrations in systems with n degrees of freedom.
2.2.1 Use of phasors for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
2.5 Spectral analysis in the time and frequency domain
Topic 3. Analysis of mechanical systems with 1 degree of freedom (DOF).
3.2 Undamped free vibrations in 1 DOF systems
3.3 Damped free vibrations in 1 DOF Systems
Topic 4. Analysis of mechanical systems with n degrees of freedom
4.3 Undamped free vibrations in n DOF systems
4.4 Undamped forced vibrations in n DOF systems
teaching_methods: Presentation of concepts and problem solving in the classroom, including discussion classes.
Personal study, report writing, practical work.
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation includes three exams and proposed exercises. Each exam must have a minimum score of 3.5 to be averaged. Exams 1 and 3 count for 25% each, Exam 2 for 30%, and mandatory proposed exercises for 20%. The final continuous evaluation grade is calculated as: 0.25*Exam1 + 0.3*Exam2 + 0.25*Exam3 + 0.2*Proposed_exercises, requiring a score of 5 or higher to pass. For the ordinary call, exams with scores above 5 are kept, and students retake only failed parts; the proposed exercises' score is kept if 5 or higher, otherwise, a new collection must be submitted. For the extraordinary call, students retake the entire course, with only the proposed exercises' score being kept if 5 or higher.
